en: The Origin of the Teaching on the *Yogācārya-śrī-mukha-dāna* (The Essential Yoga Ritual for Bestowing Food by Fire) to Ānanda;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra by Imperial Decree.
At that time, the World-Honored One was at the Nyagrodha Monastery in the city of Kapilavastu,
together with a vast assembly of bhikṣus and innumerable bodhisattvas.
He sat surrounded by those before and behind him, preaching the Dharma.
At that time, Ānanda was dwelling alone in a quiet place, reflecting upon the teachings he had received.
Then, after the third watch of that night had passed, he...
He saw a hungry ghost named Yāmukha;
its form was hideous and its body withered and emaciated.
Fire blazed from its mouth, and its throat was as narrow as the point of a needle.
With disheveled hair and long, sharp fangs and claws, he was most terrifying.
Standing before Ānanda, he said to him, "Three days from now, your life will come to an end."
"Even if one is born among the hungry ghosts.
At that time, having heard these words,
Ānanda felt fear and trepidation in his heart and asked the hungry ghost:
"O Great Being, if after my death I am reborn as a hungry ghost,
what skillful means should I now practice to escape this suffering?
At that time, the hungry ghost said to Ānanda:
On the morning of the day after tomorrow,
if you can provide food and drink for hundreds of thousands of nayutas of hungry ghosts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River,
as well as for countless other brahmins and rishis.
The food and drink consumed by the officials of the underworld presided over by Yama,
as well as by various ghosts and spirits and those who have long since passed away,
is measured by the *droṇa* used in the kingdom of Magadha.
"Give seventy-seven *hu* of food and drink to each person,
and on our behalf, make offerings to the Triple Gem;
thus you shall gain an increase in your lifespan."
"May we be freed from the suffering of hungry ghosts and be reborn in the heavens.
Ānanda saw these *yāmukha* hungry ghosts,
their bodies emaciated, withered, parched, and exceedingly hideous.
Fire blazed from their mouths and their throats were like needles;
their hair was disheveled and their fur and claws were long and sharp.
Furthermore, they heard these words:
Filled with great terror,
his body hairs all stood on end; then, at the break of dawn,
he rose from his seat and went to where the Buddha was.
Circumambulating the Buddha three times to the right, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet;
with his body trembling, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"O Greatly Compassionate World-Honored One, I pray that you will save me from my suffering."
Why is this? Last night at the third watch, while walking in meditation in a quiet place, I called to mind the Dharma I had received.
I saw a *Yamamukha* ghost who spoke to me, saying:
"In three days, your life will surely come to an end and you shall be reborn among the hungry ghosts.
I asked the ghost, "How may I escape from this suffering?"
The hungry ghost replied:
"If you can give alms to hundreds of thousands of nayutas of hungry ghosts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
as well as to the brahmins, rishis, and the officials of the realm of Yama who preside over the path of karma."
Furthermore, by universally bestowing food and drink upon all spirits, ghosts, attendants, and kinsmen, as well as those who have passed away long ago,
you shall attain an increase in your lifespan.
He addressed the World-Honored One, saying,
"How can one prepare such immeasurable food and drink as to provide for all?
The Buddha told Ānanda, "Do not be afraid now."
I recall that in the past, during immeasurable kalpas, when I was once a brahmin,
I received from the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara a dhāraṇī called the "Dhāraṇī Method of the Tathāgata Immeasurable Majestic Virtue, Sovereign Radiance."
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"If you are well able to perform this dhāraṇī rite by empowering it seven times,
you can cause a single meal to transform into various kinds of ambrosial food and drink."
It can immediately provide sufficient, exquisite food and drink for hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of hungry ghosts, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
as well as for all the various classes of brahmins, rishis, spirits, and deities.
All were fully satisfied.
Each member of this assembly likewise received a *droṇa*— the very measure used in the kingdom of Magadha.
This food and this water are equal in measure to the Dharma-realm;
though consumed, they are inexhaustible.
All who partake thereof shall attain the fruit of sainthood and liberate their bodies from suffering.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Receive and uphold this dharani method now;
it shall cause your merit, virtue, and lifespan to increase."
May those born as hungry ghosts be reborn in the heavens or pure lands to receive the bodies of devas and humans;
may this enable the donor to transform obstacles,
eliminate calamities, and prolong their years and increase their lifespan.
Manifestly inviting supreme merit, one shall realize bodhi.
Arousing the vast mind for the sake of all sentient beings—
those who have been one's parents throughout many lifetimes since time immemorial.
The celestial bureaus of the constellations, the secret offices of the underworld, and the realms of the flaming demons; all sentient beings,
down to the most minute insects and crawling creatures—
having universally prepared this vast and unobstructed offering, they have all come to attend this assembly.
Relying upon the majestic radiance of the Buddha, I cleanse the field of my body.
Having attained these supreme benefits, may I enjoy the bliss of the realms of humans and devas.
I pray only that all Buddhas, Prajñāpāramitā, Bodhisattvas, Vajra-devas, and others [will grant their protection].
As well as the immeasurable noble ones of the various paths of action,
who have realized my practice through unconditioned compassion;
therefore, we act for the sake of fulfilling our great vows.
It is for the purpose of extensively protecting and ensuring that sentient beings are saved without falling back;
for the purpose of destroying all karmic actions so they may be purified;
and for the purpose of seeking the unsurpassed path with diligence so it may be swiftly accomplished.
It is for the purpose of rescuing sentient beings in the evil realms,
so that they may forever cast off the ocean of suffering and ascend to the other shore;
as described in the sutras, this concerns the infinite worlds with their six paths and four modes of birth.
All those among them who act as sovereigns, rulers,
and leaders are bodhisattvas dwelling in the inconceivable liberation,
who have manifested transformation bodies by dividing their forms and casting shadows through the power of their compassionate vows.
They undergo suffering together with their peers within the six realms of existence.
Even when employing skillful means, they are not corrupted by the afflictions or secondary afflictions.
They discern various karmas in order to inspire the aspiration for the Way.
Constantly self-reproaching and repenting for the deeds committed by the body,
he acts as a great guide to tame and transform all sentient beings;
he destroys the three miserable realms and purifies all paths of karma.
Cutting off the stream of craving while not abandoning their vows and practices,
they act as spiritual friends within the ocean of suffering;
they bring all sentient beings to maturity for their benefit and happiness, and realize great nirvāṇa.
If there is a donor who has deep faith in the Mahāyāna and yearns for yoga,
who aspires to see and hear the nectar-like Dharma-gate of the *dhāraṇī-piṭaka*,
and who gives rise to a mind of deliverance for the sake of all sentient beings.
Heardily praising the relinquishing of great wealth and treasures,
he made three requests to the master, who then granted permission for the mandala ritual.
With equanimity and uniformity, he was free from thoughts of enmity or affection.
They constantly practice giving without regret;
they draw near to virtuous friends and apply themselves with courageous diligence, free from cowardice;
they seek the Great Way and extol the Triple Gem.
They nurture all living beings through skillful means, delivering them all to liberation.
They do not sustain their own lives through harmful pursuits,
but always benefit both themselves and others.
That son of good family is a true and virtuous friend;
practicing the bodhisattva path for the sake of all beings throughout the three miserable realms,
he acts for the benefit of all hungry ghosts within the various evil destinies.
The Brahmaṇa sages such as King Yama,
the various devas in the void including Śakra, Brahmā, and the Four Heavenly Kings,
the lunar mansions, the celestial bureaucracy, and the eight classes of nāgas and spirits.
The sun and moon, Mount Sumeru, asuras, and non-Buddhists;
the six classes of desire-realm māras, water, fire, wind, and space;
mountain forests, caves, dwellings, palaces, and monasteries.
The great earth, rivers, streams, springs, and bathing pools; temples,
omens of good and evil fortune, and wandering deities—
all these he records with unimpeded supernormal powers regarding their goodness and wickedness.
Feathered creatures fly through the air and aquatic species glide with their scales;
those with fur and horns, as well as all wriggling and sentient beings,
expose their wild souls to the elements and suffer the bitterness of having their corpses whipped.
Those bound by the enmity and resentment of many lifetimes cannot yet escape;
through kalpas, vengeful spirits carry the burden of their wealth and lives,
as do deceased monks and nuns who have not yet realized the fruits of the path.
Throughout many lifetimes, their parents, kinsmen, and relatives,
having received the teachings of the Tathāgata, were delivered from the three miserable realms;
from immeasurable hells, they gave rise to the bodhicitta.
May each of you resolve to relinquish and liberate yourselves from the bonds of enmity;
may you mutually praise and mind one another as you would think of your own parents.
Upon reaching this site of enlightenment, may you realize and receive their protective mindfulness.
The heart leaps with joy like the udumbara flower;
it is extremely difficult to encounter, being produced by one's own actions.
Abiding in the human realm, the conscious mind is difficult to stabilize.
For the most part, they follow along with delusions, accumulating them as the source of suffering;
having not yet attained the fruits of sainthood, they immediately give rise to faults and afflictions.

Furthermore, while dwelling within the sovereign’s land and water and abiding in the Buddha’s compassionate light, they constantly reflect upon past conditions and still harbor thoughts of present results.
Day and night, one should reproach oneself: "What retribution is such as this?
As for my kinsmen, relatives, and parents, how many times have they ever been fickle, perverse, or entangled in worldly attachments?"
Having changed our forms and exchanged our faces, how could we possibly recognize one another?
We only pray that today, by virtue of this Buddha’s power,
we may soar through the vast void and arrive at this place of practice.
The compassionate light brushed their bodies, and each, according to their respective form and kind,
purified their defilements and transgressions, gave rise to the bodhicitta,
and accepted these offerings.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"If you wish to receive and uphold the rite of offering food,
you must rely upon the Ācārya ritual of the profound yoga-samādhi."
Those who delight in practice should learn from a yoga-ācārya,
generate the unsurpassed mind of great awakening (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi-citta), and receive the samaya precepts.
Those who have entered the great maṇḍala and received empowerment are permitted to receive it;
they shall receive the five-wisdom empowerment of the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
Only after ascending to the rank of Acharya may one transmit the teachings.
If it is not so, each will refuse to grant permission to the other;
even if one were to practice in such a manner, they would bring calamity upon themselves.
If one commits the offense of stealing the Dharma, it will ultimately be without efficacy.
However, if one receives initiation and, relying upon the teacher’s instructions,
practices yoga according to the prescribed rules of conduct and ritual form, [success will follow].
One who is skillfully able to discern and thoroughly comprehend the characteristics of phenomena (dharmalakṣaṇa) is thus called a Tripiṭaka-master;
only such an Ācārya may transmit this teaching.
If one wishes to perform the ritual,
one must first protect oneself, and likewise protect the disciple;
this is done once the day has been ascertained.
One should select a site for a great dwelling on pure ground,
a secluded garden beloved by spirits and deities,
with flowing springs, bathing pools, rivers, seas, mountains, and marshes.
A hall for this ground of merit may also be constructed;
it should be plastered and polished according to the Dharma using fragrant clay and water,
its squareness, roundness, or size depending on the power and resources of the patron.
Erect banners at the four corners, adorning them according to the ritual rules.
Use five-colored silks to place flaming jewels upon them.
Furthermore, within these jewels, install the Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa, Mahākaruṇā, Pratisarā, and Uṣṇīṣavijayā.
Uṣṇīṣavijayā in the northeast;
Mahākaruṇā in the southeast;
and Parṇaśavarī in the southwest.
In the northwest is Uṣṇīṣavijayā.
Furthermore, the four pillars are adorned according to the ritual rules;
they are exceptionally wonderful and beautiful, known as the Auspicious Banners (Śrīvatsadhvaja).
It causes an area of one hundred yojanas to be free from all decline and affliction,
thereby establishing a boundary (sīmā).
This is accomplished by the blowing of wind, the brushing of shadows, the scattering of earth, and the moistening with water.
Their karmic obstructions shall be extinguished and they shall obtain great benefit and merit;
all who see with their eyes or hear with their ears shall universally receive relief and succor.
Furthermore, one should subsequently suspend silk streamers, banners, and canopies around the perimeter.
Jeweled fans and white whisks were arranged in their respective positions;
there were fragrant *āguru* water, exquisite flowers, lamps, and ointments;
as well as food, drink, medicinal decoctions, various fruits and flavors, and other such items.
Purify them with the Dharma so that they are not defiled by impurities.
Once the adornments are complete, hold a fragrant incense burner in your hands and circumambulate the site of practice (maṇḍala) to the right, observing it thoroughly with insight.
Wherever there are deficiencies, they should be carefully arranged.
Once the rites of adornment are completed, together with his disciples,
he bathes in fragrant water and puts on fresh, clean garments.
Go outside to the central courtyard and sweep it according to the ritual rules.
Anoint the ground with fragrant mud and adorn it according to the ritual rules;
this is called the *samaya* mandala.
Outside the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), spread out a clean mat of grass and arrange one’s deportment with solemnity.
Perform three prostrations, kneel with the right knee on the ground facing east,
and holding an incense burner in hand, perform the rite of invocation.
The Account of Ānanda Regarding the Origin of the Teaching on the *Yogacaryābhūmi-saṃgraha-yamāntaka-bali* is hereby concluded.
